drug_class: Thiazolidinedione (TZD) — a type of oral diabetes medicine
purpose: Pioglitazone is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is usually used along with diet, exercise, and sometimes other diabetes medicines. It helps your body use insulin more effectively so your blood sugar stays in a healthier range.
how_it_works: Your body has special receptors in fat, muscle, and liver cells that help control how well insulin works. Pioglitazone activates these receptors, making your body's cells more sensitive and responsive to insulin. Think of it like unlocking a door that allows sugar to enter your cells properly instead of building up in your blood.
common_side_effects: Weight gain and fluid retention (swelling in your legs or ankles) are the most common side effects. You may also notice mild cold or upper respiratory symptoms, headache, or muscle pain. Some people notice their blood sugar can drop (hypoglycemia), especially if taking other diabetes medicines alongside this one.
warnings: Pioglitazone can cause or worsen heart failure — tell your doctor right away if you notice sudden weight gain, swelling, or shortness of breath. It has also been linked to a small increased risk of bladder cancer with long-term use, so tell your doctor about any blood in your urine. It should NOT be used if you already have heart failure. Women who have not yet reached menopause should know this medicine can increase the chance of pregnancy. It can also increase the risk of bone fractures, especially in women.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 15 mg or 30 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Your doctor may increase your dose up to a maximum of 45 mg per day depending on how well your blood sugar is controlled. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep a steady level in your body.
